TASK: Build the error-state routing truth table for the booking write path of a Bland AI conversational pathway, from the graph JSON alone. This lane answers: which gateway responses reach e_booking_failed, which reach e_safe_failure, which fall through, and whether a 502 is distinguishable from a genuine failure in the routing conditions at all.

INCIDENT CONTEXT. This pathway is a Bland AI SMS agent (pathway version 87: 42 nodes, 115 edges, 12 Webhook nodes, 11 End Call nodes) that books eye-exam appointments through a self-hosted gateway at https://mott-booking-gw.mail.mybcat.com. On 2026-08-03 a patient confirmed a booking, the pathway replied "I couldn't confirm that booking" (End node e_booking_failed), and the appointment WAS created in the EMR anyway. Measured facts: the gateway's /sign write endpoint returned HTTP 502 {"error":"gateway_unreachable","status":502} in 28.2s while the write committed; the platform recorded BlandStatusCode: 502 and the conversation ended at e_booking_failed. A 502 on /sign means the outcome is UNKNOWN, not failed. The gateway also returns structured errors 423 {"error":"write_unverified"} and 403 {"error":"authorization_denied"}. Full incident packet (read-only source material): /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/EVIDENCE-502.md.

PATHWAY JSON STRUCTURE (verified against the actual file — trust these field names): The file /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/pathway-v87.json is a JSON object with keys nodes, edges, analysis_options, entity_schemas, etc. Each node has id, type ('Default' | 'Webhook' | 'End Call'), and data. Webhook node data has: url, method, body, headers, responseData (list of {"name": <variable>, "data": <JSONPath like $.success>}), responsePathways (ORDERED list of 4-element condition entries [variable, operator, value, {"id": <destination node id>, "name": <label>}]), and modelOptions.retryAttempts. Default node data has a prompt field; End Call node data has text, outcome, and name. Some node data carries isStart, isGlobal, and globalLabel. The top-level edges array mirrors all routing: each edge has source, target, and data.label (the condition or LLM-routing description). For Webhook nodes the edges duplicate responsePathways one-to-one (47 responsePathways entries, 47 webhook-sourced edges).

ANALYZE these four webhook nodes: n_book_1 and n_book_2 (POST /sign, the appointment write) and n_verify_1 and n_verify_2 (POST /conflict-check, the pre-write verification). For each, transcribe its responsePathways EXACTLY as they appear in the JSON (same order, same variable names, same operators, same values, destination = the entry's id field) and its outgoing edges from the top-level edges array. Then reason about where each class of gateway response actually routes. The gateway response classes to trace, using the response contracts in the catalog at /home/ankit114/.claude/skills/bland-ai/catalogs/mott-aws-webhooks.json and the incident packet: (1) HTTP 200 {"success": true, "new_appt_id": ...}; (2) a response with success false and no recognized error code; (3) {"error": "slot_conflict"}; (4) HTTP 502 {"error":"gateway_unreachable","status":502} — note this body has NO success key, so what does the extracted book_success variable hold?; (5) HTTP 423 {"error":"write_unverified"}; (6) HTTP 403 {"error":"authorization_denied"}; (7) a network timeout / empty response where no variables extract at all. For each class state the destination node under Bland's ordered condition evaluation, or 'fallthrough_unknown' if no condition can match and the platform default is not determinable from the export. Be explicit about how missing JSONPath extractions behave in conditions (empty vs undefined) and mark what is inference vs fact. The incident is evidence: a real 502 DID end at e_booking_failed, so your table must be consistent with that observation or explain why not.

Also enumerate every edge whose target is e_safe_failure (the 'gateway_failed' End node) and answer directly: does ANY response from the /sign write nodes route to e_safe_failure, either directly (an edge from n_book_1/n_book_2) or transitively (any path)? If the distinction between 'gateway unreachable' and 'booking failed' exists in the End nodes but no write-path response can reach the safe one, say so plainly.

OUTPUT 1 — truth-table.json in your working directory, EXACTLY this shape (a verifier parses it and cross-checks every mechanical claim against the pathway JSON, so transcribe, do not paraphrase):
{
  "nodes": {"n_book_1": {"response_pathways": [{"variable": ..., "operator": ..., "value": ..., "destination": <node id>}, ... in JSON order], "edges": [{"target": ..., "label": <edge data.label>}]}, "n_book_2": {...}, "n_verify_1": {...}, "n_verify_2": {...}},
  "scenarios": [{"scenario_id": <see list below>, "response_class": <short description>, "variables_after_extraction": {<variable>: <value or "ABSENT">}, "destination": <node id or "fallthrough_unknown">, "destination_reasoning": <at least 120 chars>}, ...],
  "e_safe_failure_inbound": [<every edge source whose target is e_safe_failure>],
  "e_safe_failure_reachable_from_booking_write": {"direct_route_from_book_nodes": <bool>, "transitive_route_exists": <bool>, "explanation": <at least 150 chars>},
  "verdict_502_distinguishable": {"verdict": "yes"|"no"|"partial", "explanation": <at least 200 chars>}
}
Required scenario_id values (all seven, exactly these strings): success_true, success_false_no_error_code, slot_conflict, http_502_gateway_unreachable, http_423_write_unverified, http_403_authorization_denied, timeout_or_empty_response.

OUTPUT 2 — truth-table.md: a human-readable report of the same findings for a reviewer watching a dashboard: the truth table as a Markdown table, the e_safe_failure answer, and the 502-distinguishability verdict with your reasoning.

READ-ONLY BOUNDARY (non-negotiable): You must not modify pathway-v87.json or any other source file. You must not call any live API, gateway, webhook, or network endpoint of any kind — this is a static analysis of a JSON export on disk. Write ONLY into your own task working directory (your current working directory when you start). You are stateless: nobody can answer questions. If something is genuinely undeterminable from the files provided, write that in the report explicitly instead of guessing.
tasks.verified: The transcribed routing conditions and edges of n_book_1/n_book_2/n_verify_1/n_verify_2 match pathway-v87.json exactly, the e_safe_failure inbound set and its (non-)reachability from the book nodes match an independent recomputation, and all seven gateway-response scenarios plus the 502-distinguishability verdict are present with substantive reasoning.

Find: nodes unreachable from the start node, End nodes no edge ever targets, nodes with no path to any End node, and routing conditions that can never match. Keep the mechanical layer (pure edge-graph computation) strictly separate from the judgment layer (Bland global-node semantics, condition shadowing), because a verifier recomputes the mechanical layer independently and your numbers must match it exactly.

IMPORTANT SEMANTICS: Some nodes have data.isGlobal == true with a data.globalLabel describing when the platform may jump to them from ANYWHERE in the conversation. A node with zero inbound edges is therefore not necessarily unreachable — it may be a global entry point. COMPUTE the mechanical layer over the top-level edges array only (directed source -> target): (a) the start node — the node whose data.isStart is true; (b) edges_only_unreachable_from_start — every node id not reachable from the start node by following edges; (c) zero_inbound_edge_end_nodes — every End Call node that no edge targets; (d) edges_only_no_path_to_end — every node from which no End Call node can be reached by following edges. Then the judgment layer: (e) global_nodes — every node with isGlobal true, each with a sentence on how it changes real reachability; (f) effectively_unreachable — the subset of the edges-only-unreachable nodes that remain unreachable even after accounting for global entry (a global node itself is never in this list), each with a reason; (g) condition_order_review — for EACH of the 12 Webhook nodes, examine its ORDERED responsePathways and judge whether any later condition is shadowed by an earlier one that necessarily matches first (verdict no_shadowing, shadowed, or cannot_determine, with the reason); (h) never_match_conditions — any condition, on any node, that can never be true given how its variable is produced (e.g. a variable that no responseData entry and no upstream node ever sets, or a value the producing endpoint can never return per the catalog at /home/ankit114/.claude/skills/bland-ai/catalogs/mott-aws-webhooks.json). Empty list if you find none — do not invent findings.

OUTPUT 1 — reachability.json in your working directory, EXACTLY this shape:
{
  "start_node": <node id>,
  "edges_only_unreachable_from_start": [<node ids, may be empty>],
  "zero_inbound_edge_end_nodes": [<End Call node ids>],
  "edges_only_no_path_to_end": [<node ids, may be empty>],

  "never_match_conditions": [{"node": <node id>, "condition": <the condition as text>, "why_never_matches": <at least 60 chars>}, ... may be empty]
}
